facts.text: Mount Nelson opened on Monday, 6 March 1899.
facts.excerpt: Mount Nelson opens on Monday, 6 March.

facts.text: The second manager, Aldo Renato, painted the hotel pink in 1918 to celebrate the end of the First World War.
facts.excerpt: celebrated the end of the First World War by painting the hotel pink

facts.text: Mount Nelson was the first hotel in South Africa to offer hot and cold running water.
facts.excerpt: The first hotel in South Africa to offer hot and cold running water

facts.text: A row of eight restored historic cottages on the grounds was converted into the Garden Cottage Suites in 1990.
facts.excerpt: A row of eight perfectly restored historic cottages on the hotel grounds were converted into the elegantly appointed Garden Cottage Suites.

facts.text: The wooden chairs in the Garden Room and the Lord Nelson Room were originally deck chairs on Union-Castle Line ships.
facts.excerpt: The wooden chairs in the Garden Room and the Lord Nelson Room today were originally used as deck chairs on the Union-Castle Line ships.

facts.text: Planet Bar spills out onto an outdoor terrace overlooking the gardens.
facts.excerpt: it spilled out onto the expansive outdoor terrace, overlooking the glorious gardens.

facts.text: Librisa Spa is a day spa offering treatments in a historic Victorian house.
facts.excerpt: An elegant destination day spa offering modern treatments in a sublime historic Victorian house

facts.text: The Red Room by Chefs Warehouse, by chef Liam Tomlin, serves Pan-Asian cuisine in the underground space formerly known as The Grill Room.
facts.excerpt: Liam Tomlin opens The Red Room by Chefs Warehouse at Mount Nelson, a retro sophisticated celebration of Pan-Asian cuisines in the legendary underground space formerly known as The Grill Room.

facts.text: Afternoon Tea has been served on the Windsor Table in the Hotel Lounge since 1989; before that it was served from a tea trolley.
facts.excerpt: Afternoon Tea is served on the Windsor Table in the Hotel Lounge for the first time ever on 1 November. It had previously been served from a tea trolley.

facts.text: The Company's Garden, South Africa's oldest public gardens, is located across Orange Street from the hotel.
The Prince of Wales Gate and palm-lined driveway were built in 1924 in honour of a visit by the Prince of Wales.
facts.excerpt: The grand ‘Prince of Wales Gate’ and palm-lined driveway was built the year before in honour of this visit.

facts.text: The Oasis wing was added to the main house in 1973.
facts.excerpt: The Oasis wing was added to Mount Nelson’s main house.
